I implemented JIT-compatible fixed-size variants of `masked_select` and `nonzero` in `tinygrad/tensor.py`.

**`masked_select(self, mask, size=None, fill_value=0)`**
- `size=None`: unchanged behavior (dynamic length via `.item()`).

Rows stay contiguous in the flattened selection, so fill/truncation land on clean row boundaries. Output is always `dtypes.default_int` regardless of a float `fill_value`.
